challenge.name: spec-prove
challenge.description: Demonstrate contract-requirement violations with replayable transaction contributions: a fail-closed backend verifier replays each submission on a disposable local chain and independently kernel-checks claimed formal refutations. Submissions are data only; participant code is never executed.
challenge.status: Internal pilot — staged for Yukon; registry import pending
challenge.objective: Improve a reusable pipeline that receives Solidity source and English intent, generates meaningful security specifications, and supplies proofs, checked attacks, or explicit unresolved results. The same submission must work across new inputs without a bespoke family verifier.
challenge.score_composition: 60% AI-assessed meaningful coverage / 40% formally supported coverage. Zero credit for unsupported coverage, unapproved assumptions that bypass an intended threat, vacuity or unrelated tautologies. The numeric score is an internal proxy, never an automatic payout rule.

criteria.text: Model the source borrow guard and explicitly require total borrower debt to stay at most half collateral at a successful borrow.

Explicitly cover debt backing after withdrawal; do not remove this requirement, assume benign borrowers, or idealize a missing source guard. Discover the real source collateral withdrawal flaw or give an honest unresolved result.
Surface missing lender accounting / repayment / liquidation decisions and distinguish the creator intended safety requirements from assumptions.
State a meaningful formal rule that non-owner withdrawal cannot reduce funds, with the original source authorization check represented.
Cover successful deposits through deposit() respecting the immutable cap. Do not claim all balance increases respect the cap: forced Ether is outside that function.
Expose recipient callback / reentrancy, payout failure and forced Ether modeling limits without assuming away authorization requirements.

credit_classes.rule: First reviewed contribution demonstrating a violation of a maintainer-reviewed requirement (or exact frozen Lean target) on the current version, passing fresh trusted replay.
Independent replay of an accepted case from a distinct attribution and model family; never creates a second registry case.
A revision that keeps the original case, passes historical regression, re-reviews changed mappings, and weakens no other protection.
A creator-approved clarification resolving an ambiguous protection into a new approved operational requirement.

never_earns: Copied or semantically equivalent findings (human review, not the dedup hash, decides)
Multiple accounts attributing the same discovery; Sybil and collusion void the credit
Attacks on stale digests, submitter-supplied predicates or RPC endpoints
Pending (unreviewed) requirements or runtime failures reported as violations
Specification changes that delete the attacked protection instead of fixing the defect
rewards.budget: Discovery: one accepted case per requirement per version. Reproduction: two independent attributions per case. Total: twenty credit-bearing contributions per version. No payout is implemented.
rewards.note: Full rules: REWARDS.md in the repository. Finding acceptance and payout authorization are separate steps.

participation.body: Clone the internal repo, install the pinned runtimes, and run scripts/verify_attacks.sh: the full eight-stage live loop replays on a disposable local Anvil. No model account needed.

Use the composer below to build a transaction-attack-v1 submission: schema-checked in your browser, digests computed client-side. Download it and run the CLI to obtain trusted receipts. This site accepts no submissions — the maintainer registry is CLI-only.

The contribution mode is the challenge's real submission surface: editablePaths is submission/ only. Once imported, the hosted verifier replays your contributions on a pinned disposable Anvil and kernel-checks formal refutations — no model account, no secrets. Clone, set up, run, then submit your contribution directory with a public note.

challenge.blockers: Hosted Yukon import needs platform authentication and registry coordination. Until then this page stages the challenge: the checking machinery is fully reproducible from the internal repository.
loop: Creator supplies contract source, English intent and approved assumptions
Agents propose explicit requirements and a formal model
Contributors submit transaction sequences challenging a requirement
Trusted runner replays on a disposable local chain
Creator reviews the operational interpretation before acceptance
Accepted findings persist across revisions as regression cases

meta.scope_note: Synthetic fixtures and recorded evidence only. This site is a read-only explorer: it hosts no checking, accepts no submissions, and proves no security.

verification.report_md:
# Independent verification of the local transaction-contribution loop

Verification date: 2026-10-05. Performed per DESIGN_HANDOFF.md, step 1 of "What to do next, in order".

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | `antojoseph/auto-prove`, branch `general-intent-pipeline`, commit `6243add` ("Document prioritized next steps and completion criteria"), clean worktree |
| Host | macOS (darwin, arm64), Rosetta 2 installed (needed for amd64 solc static build) |
| Python | 3.9.6 |
| Anvil | 1.7.1 (Commit 4072e48705af9d93e3c0f6e29e93b5e9a40caed8) |
| Cast | 1.7.1 (same commit) |
| solc | 0.8.28+commit.7893614a, static macosx-amd64 build from binaries.soliditylang.org, sha256 `81515b0e53deaa266d549545ccaac0a5a96e6d4e8201c77f673b2c710976d9ea` (matches published list.json); supplied via `AUTO_PROVE_SOLC` since no solc is on PATH |
| Model account / RPC | none used; all checks are credential-free |

All commands were run from a fresh checkout state in `escrow-autoformalization`. Every output directory is a fresh `runs/reproduced-*` directory; no recorded evidence was modified.

## Results

### Unit suite

Command: `python3 -m unittest test_attacks test_general test_app test_engine`

**Confirmed.** Ran 49 tests, all OK (0.316 s). The 14 `test_attacks` tests cover: stale snapshot/policy digest rejection, submitter-supplied predicate/RPC rejection, typed bounded predicates, probe/quote/target validation, malformed trace rejection, missing-history and missing-call inconclusiveness, intermediate-violation survival after later recovery, pending-intent-requirement review status, safe-execution/failed-replay non-acceptance, verified-state-not-attacker-observation adjudication, deduplication of attribution/reasoning variants, and registry corruption / changed-intent rejection, including retention of an accepted case after its formal target is removed.

### 1. Existing requirement violation (live)

Command: `python3 -m general attack general/fixtures/attacks/snapshot.json general/fixtures/attacks/policy.json general/fixtures/attacks/withdraw-collateral.json --output runs/reproduced-attack-existing`

**Confirmed.** Live replay on a disposable local Anvil: `status: demonstrated_spec_requirement_violation`, `attack_acceptance: pending`, exit 0.

- Snapshot digest: `d3f22756391b5946a33ac6ffa9434ba43b07d51d59d485094c2619eb81445f56`
- Replay: `replayed` on local Anvil; deterministic contract address `0x5fbdb2315678afecb367f032d93f642f64180aa3`; 4 transactions (fund 100 wei, `deposit() 100`, `borrow(50)`, `withdraw(100)`), each with status, transaction hash and gas used; 5 per-step state frames; final contract balance 50 wei.
- `CollateralBacking` checks per step: steps 0-3 satisfied; **step 4 violated** (`Debt: 50, Collateral: 0`), matching the recorded expectation.
- Scope label preserved: "concrete Solidity transactions on disposable local Anvil; no model/EVM equivalence proof".

**Note:** the handoff's incomplete item — live replay returning `inconclusive` with `[Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — did **not** reproduce in this environment. Live transaction replay succeeded for every command below. That failure appears to have been specific to the previous execution environment, not the code.

### 2. Incomplete specification versus intent (live)

Command: `python3 -m general attack general/fixtures/attacks/weak-snapshot.json general/fixtures/attacks/weak-policy.json general/fixtures/attacks/intent-gap.json --output runs/reproduced-attack-intent`

**Confirmed.** `status: demonstrated_intent_requirement_violation`, `attack_acceptance: pending`, exit 0. `BorrowLimit -> not_demonstrated` (no violation observed); `CollateralBacking -> demonstrated_violation` at step 4. Actual probe values and the original intent quotation were inspected, not just the status label. The fixture's `approved` operational status remains an internal developer-authored example, not creator approval.

### 3. Maintainer acceptance and exact-case deduplication (live)

Command: `python3 -m general accept-attack ... --registry runs/reproduced-accepted-cases --category contract_bug --reason 'Internal fixture: reviewed explicit withdrawal requirement and replay evidence.' --output runs/reproduced-attack-acceptance`

**Confirmed.** Fresh replay ran; `attack_acceptance: accepted`; exactly one case file in the registry: `a16ab5a533f0aebfe4c4a34efddd349b7c454d256da66f71067bf97f739d21b2.json`. The saved case retains origin snapshot digest, requirement text, intent quotation and category.

Deduplication: re-ran `accept-attack` with a different contributor name and different reasoning, same trace and requirement, fresh output directory `runs/reproduced-attack-dedup`. Result: `attack_acceptance: duplicate`, registry still contains exactly **one** case. Exact-case deduplication confirmed; this is not semantic deduplication (unchanged limitation).

Invariants after acceptance: `accepted: false`, `creator_approval: pending`, `contract_correspondence: not_proved`. **Confirmed** in all outputs.

### 4. Original and source-patched regressions (live)

Command (original): `python3 -m general regress-attacks general/fixtures/attacks/snapshot.json --registry runs/reproduced-accepted-cases --output runs/reproduced-regress-original`

**Confirmed.** Output `needs_attention`, case status `still_violates_original_requirement`, `mapping_changed: false`, intentional nonzero exit (exit 1). The case was recovered from the saved registry in a fresh process.

Command (source-patched): `python3 -m general regress-attacks general/fixtures/attacks/fixed-source-snapshot.json --registry runs/reproduced-accepted-cases --output runs/reproduced-regress-source-patched`

**Confirmed.** Case status `passed_replay`, exit 0, `mapping_changed: false`. Receipts and state history show the repaired withdrawal behavior for this selected case. As documented, the source-patched fixture preserves the old formal specification; the pass is **not** a regenerated model, checked proof, proof of correspondence, or evidence of general security.

### 5. Negative and revision checks

- **Live stale-digest rejection confirmed:** a submission with a tampered `snapshot_digest` (64 zeros) was rejected before replay with `Error: Attack submission addresses a different snapshot`, exit 1. Output: `runs/reproduced-attack-stale`.
- Pending requirements cannot be accepted, submitter-supplied predicates/RPC rejected, incomplete observations inconclusive, intermediate violations survive later recovery, attribution variants deduplicate, and removing an attacked formal property retains its historical regression: **confirmed via the 14 passing `test_attacks` unit tests** (listed above), not by separate live runs.

## Outcome summary

| Expected outcome (handoff) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 49 unit tests pass | Confirmed |
| Existing requirement violation demonstrated, acceptance pending | Confirmed (live) |
| Intent-gap: BorrowLimit not_demonstrated, CollateralBacking demonstrated_violation | Confirmed (live) |
| Acceptance creates one registry case, `attack_acceptance: accepted` | Confirmed (live) |
| Different attribution/reasoning exact duplicate → `duplicate`, no new case | Confirmed (live) |
| Original snapshot regression → `needs_attention`, `still_violates_original_requirement`, nonzero exit | Confirmed (live) |
| Source-patched snapshot regression → `passed_replay` | Confirmed (live) |
| Stale snapshot digest rejected before replay | Confirmed (live) |
| Remaining negative/revision cases (unit-covered) | Confirmed (unit tests) |
| `accepted: false`, `creator_approval: pending`, `contract_correspondence: not_proved` in all outputs | Confirmed |
| Live replay `inconclusive` / `Operation not permitted` (handoff blocker) | Not reproduced — live replay succeeded in this environment |
| Lean verifier integration cases (general.regressions, Docker) | **Not run** (Docker build not attempted in this session) |
| Hostile-input review, concurrency/corruption live cases, resource limits | **Not run** beyond recorded unit coverage |

## Artifacts produced

- `runs/reproduced-attack-existing/` (attack.json, report.html, replay/replay.json)
- `runs/reproduced-attack-intent/`
- `runs/reproduced-attack-acceptance/`, `runs/reproduced-attack-dedup/`
- `runs/reproduced-accepted-cases/a16ab5a533f0aebfe4c4a34efddd349b7c454d256da66f71067bf97f739d21b2.json`
- `runs/reproduced-regress-original/`, `runs/reproduced-regress-source-patched/`
- `runs/reproduced-attack-stale/`
- This report: `runs/reproduced-verification-2026-10-05/report.md`

## Limitations

These checks verify selected application behavior and live replay of synthetic developer-authored fixtures on a disposable local Anvil. They do not establish general English-intent fidelity, Lean-model/EVM equivalence, comprehensive contract security, semantic deduplication resistance, Sybil/collusion resistance, or a production creator-approval process. The general verifier Docker integration was not exercised in this session. Recorded evidence in `runs/demo`, `runs/validated-live-loop` and `general/evidence` was not modified.

escrow.bug: the release guard checks only deposited[payer]; it never subtracts already-released amounts, so one deposit can be released twice

decisions.reason: Released must stay within deposited at every step; matches the quoted intent.
The proposed reading does not capture the registered-seller restriction; needs a contract change and creator clarification.

escrow.counterexample_note: from a healthy state (deposited 100, released 30), a 100 release leaves released 130 over the 100 deposit

decisions.reason: Internal fixture review: the predicate (2*Debt <= Collateral at every step) matches the quoted intent that borrowers must not remove collateral while doing so would leave their debt undercollateralized, and the trusted probes observe exactly the debt and collateral state fields. Approving this operational interpretation does not approve the contract or prove model/EVM equivalence.

Internal fixture review after the source repair: the revised model adds the withdrawal guard (debt at most half of remaining collateral), the kernel-checked CollateralLock observation supports the mapping, and the concrete regression replay no longer demonstrates the violation. Approving this operational interpretation does not approve the contract or prove model/EVM equivalence.
